sheets.title: National movement 1885 – 1918
sheets.intro: Associations, Congress founding, Moderates, Swadeshi, Extremists, revolutionaries, Home Rule.

keys.name: Associations before 1885

rows.v: 1876 – S.N. Banerjee, Ananda Mohan Bose (ICS age protest)
1884 – Veeraraghavachariar, G. Subramania Iyer, Ananda Charlu

traps: East India Association was in London

rows.v: 28 Dec 1885; Gokuldas Tejpal Sanskrit College, Bombay (moved from Poona – cholera)
A.O. Hume (Indian National Union 1884; name from Naoroji); president W.C. Bonnerjee; 72 delegates
Safety valve (Lajpat Rai, 1916) vs lightning conductor (founders used Hume)
Muslim president Tyabji 1887; English president George Yule 1888; woman speaker Kadambini Ganguly 1890; Andhra president Ananda Charlu (Nagpur 1891)

keys.name: Moderates

rows.v: Naoroji ("Grand Old Man"; first Indian MP 1892, Finsbury), Gokhale (Servants of India 1905; Gandhi's guru), Ranade (Gokhale's guru), S.N. Banerjee (Bengalee; "Rashtraguru"), Pherozeshah Mehta (Bombay Chronicle 1913), Dinshaw Wacha, R.C. Dutt (Economic History of India)
Petitions, speeches – "political mendicancy", 3 Ps (prayer, petition, protest)
Indian ICS, less army spending, bigger councils, rights – self-rule within Empire
Naoroji – Poverty and Un-British Rule in India (1901)
Indian Councils Act 1892 – budget discussion, indirect election

traps: 1892 Act allowed budget discussion, not voting

rows.v: R.M. Sayani; Vande Mataram first sung
R.C. Dutt; drain, fixed land revenue
Eastern Bengal and Assam (Dacca) vs Bengal
Boycott resolution, Calcutta Town Hall 7 Aug 1905; 16 Oct mourning, Raksha Bandhan, "Amar Sonar Bangla" (Tagore)
Delhi Durbar 12 Dec 1911 (Hardinge II); capital to Delhi
National Council of Education 15 Aug 1906; Bengal National College (Aurobindo principal); Bengal Technical Institute
P.C. Ray – Bengal Chemicals; V.O. Chidambaram Pillai – Swadeshi Steam Navigation, Tuticorin 1906
Swadesh Bandhab (Ashwini Kumar Dutta, Barisal), Brati, Suhrid, Anushilan
Punjab – Lajpat Rai, Ajit Singh; Madras – V.O.C.; Maharashtra – Tilak; Andhra – Vandemataram movement (Bipin Pal's tour 1907)
By 1908 – repression, Surat split; Muslim peasants not reached

keys.name: Extremists (Lal – Bal – Pal)

rows.v: Moderate failure; 1896 – 97 famine, plague; Japan beat Russia 1905; Curzon (Calcutta Corporation Act 1899, Official Secrets Act 1904, Universities Act 1904)

Kesari, Mahratta (1881); Ganapati (1893), Shivaji (1895) festivals; "Swaraj is my birthright"; sedition 1897; Mandalay 1908 – 14 – Gita Rahasya; Arctic Home in the Vedas; "Father of Indian Unrest" (Chirol)
"Punjab Kesari"; deported 1907 with Ajit Singh; Punjab National Bank; Home Rule League of America 1917; Servants of the People 1921
New India, Paridarshak; "Father of revolutionary thoughts"
Bande Mataram daily; passive resistance; acquitted in Alipore case; Pondicherry 1910

traps: Punjab Kesari = Lajpat Rai; Andhra Kesari = Prakasam

rows.v: Dacca, 30 Dec 1906; Nawab Salimullah; first president Aga Khan; Jinnah joined 1913
Indian Councils Act 1909 – separate Muslim electorates; councils up to 60 extra; S.P. Sinha first Indian in Viceroy's council
Naoroji – Swaraj, Swadeshi, Boycott, National Education

keys.name: Surat split

rows.v: Extremists lost faith in Moderates; fight over 1906 resolutions and president
Allahabad Convention 1908 – Extremists kept out; Congress constitution 1908
Seditious Meetings Act 1907; Newspapers Act 1908; Press Act 1910

traps: Rash Behari Ghosh (Congress) ≠ Rash Behari Bose (revolutionary)

rows.v: Calcutta 1902 (Pramatha Mitra); Dacca branch – Pulin Behari Das
30 Apr 1908 – Khudiram Bose, Prafulla Chaki (target Kingsford); Khudiram hanged
Bomb on Hardinge, 23 Dec 1912 – Rash Behari Bose, Basant Kumar Biswas
London 1905 – Shyamji Krishna Varma; Indian Sociologist

keys.name: Ghadar party

rows.v: Sohan Singh Bhakna (president), Lala Har Dayal, Kartar Singh Sarabha (hanged 1915), Rash Behari Bose
1914; Gurdit Singh; turned back at Vancouver; Budge Budge firing
Rising 21 Feb 1915 – betrayed; Singapore 5th Light Infantry mutiny

traps: Ghadar HQ San Francisco, not London

keys.name: Home Rule Leagues

rows.v: April 1916, Belgaum – Maharashtra, Karnataka, CP, Berar
Sept 1916, Adyar – rest of India; New India, Commonweal; interned June 1917
Montagu's August Declaration, 20 Aug 1917 – responsible government by stages

traps: Tilak’s League first (April), Besant’s in September

rows.v: Congress accepted separate electorates; joint reform demand – Tilak and Jinnah

keys.name: Congress sessions 1906 – 1918

rows.v: B.N. Dar – Jana Gana Mana first sung

traps: Vande Mataram 1896, Jana Gana Mana 1911 – both Calcutta

rows.v: 1868, Jessore – Ghosh brothers; turned English 1878 to dodge VPA
Vernacular Press Act 1878 (Lytton; repealed 1882); Newspapers Act 1908; Press Act 1910
